references.text: Abdon had forty sons and thirty grandsons who rode on seventy donkey foals, showing a similar pattern of many sons riding donkeys as a sign of wealth and status.
Reference to those who ride on white donkeys, indicating high social status in Israel at that time.
Jair, son of Manasseh, captured villages and named them Havvoth-Jair (the villages of Jair), which is the same naming mentioned in Judges 10:4.
Jair, son of Manasseh, took the entire region of Argob and called it Havvoth-Jair after his own name, which is the background for the village names in Judges 10:4.
Havvoth-Jair is mentioned as part of Gilead's territory, confirming the geographical location of Jair's villages.
